title: Routing: stage-based traffic splitting / partition selection for Dedicated pool staged rollouts (multi-region)
creator: Mina Haddad
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
content:
Context / problem
Dedicated customers need staged rollouts (0/1/10/50/100 or replica partitions) to safely introduce new model versions, runtime builds, routing policies, etc. Control plane will publish a rollout plan with a current stage; routing must deterministically steer some fraction of Dedicated traffic to the canary/stage partition while protecting baseline capacity and handling multi-region pools.

This ticket covers the routing + data plane changes to support stage-based traffic splitting / partition selection for Dedicated pools.

Goals
- Implement stage-based traffic splitting for Dedicated pools driven by DedicatedPoolRolloutPlan.current_stage.
- Support both:
  (a) traffic-percentage stages (e.g., 1%, 10%, 50%, 100%)
  (b) replica/partition stages (explicit canary partition size) where percentage is not feasible (small pools)
- Deterministic routing decision (same input -> same partition choice) to avoid request flapping and to allow reliable measurement.
- Multi-region correctness: keep behavior consistent across regions while honoring regional capacity/health.
- Safe fallback behavior when canary partition is unhealthy/saturated or capacity is insufficient.
- Observability hooks: emit labels/tags so telemetry can attribute per-stage (stage_id, partition, pool_id, region).

Non-goals
- Fully general A/B experimentation for Dedicated outside rollout safety.
- Per-customer arbitrary custom routing predicates for v1.

References
- Confluence design spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/staged-rollouts-for-dedicated-pools-design-spec.json
- ADR (stage model): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-dedicated-rollout-stage-model.json
- ADR (rollback/abort semantics): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-rollback-and-abort-semantics-for-dedicated-rollouts.json
- Infra partitioning guidelines: sources/confluence/eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity/dedicated-pool-partitioning-guidelines-for-staged-rollouts.json

Functional requirements / acceptance criteria
1) Routing inputs
- Router receives (directly or via cached control-plane snapshot) these fields per Dedicated pool:
  - rollout_state: draft|running|held|aborted|completed
  - stage_id + stage definition:
    - percent_traffic OR replica_partition
    - stage constraints: min_headroom, min_replicas (if replica-based)
  - stable target (baseline partition) + canary target (new version/runtime/config)
  - multi_region_policy: split within region first; avoid cross-region unless explicitly allowed by existing Dedicated policy

2) Deterministic assignment
- Requests must be assigned to canary vs stable deterministically.
- v1 approach:
  - If request has session_id / conversation_id: hash(session_id, stage_id, pool_id) to pick partition.
  - Else: hash(request_id, stage_id, pool_id) (note: request_id-based hashing will distribute but not “stick” across requests; acceptable for stateless endpoints).
  - For streaming: decision is made at request start and pinned for duration of stream.

3) Multi-region behavior
- Primary rule: decide region using existing Dedicated region selection (closest/affinity) THEN apply stage split within the chosen region.
- If chosen region has no canary capacity (e.g., not yet provisioned, or drained), behavior must be:
  - Prefer stable in-region, rather than shifting canary traffic cross-region.
  - Only cross-region for canary if Dedicated pool is configured for cross-region spillover AND the stage definition allows it (explicit allowlist in plan config).
- If a region becomes impaired mid-stage:
  - For new requests: route to stable in healthy regions per existing failover, but treat canary as unavailable unless canary is healthy in failover region.
  - Avoid partial region exposure where one region is on canary and another is not, unless the rollout plan is explicitly region-scoped (future).

4) Safety + fallback
- Canary selection must be guarded by:
  - partition health (node/GPU health + service readiness)
  - saturation/headroom checks (queue depth, 429 rate, utilization thresholds)
- On canary unhealthy/saturated:
  - Route to stable partition (same region if possible) and emit a “canary_bypassed” metric/log.
  - Do NOT exceed the advertised canary percentage by rerouting stable->canary retries.
- Protection against starvation: canary should never steal capacity reserved for stable such that stable 429s spike. Enforce min_headroom for stable partition when stage is active.

5) Rollback/abort interactions
- If rollout is aborted/rolled back (stage moves backward or rollout_state=aborted): routing should stop sending new requests to canary immediately.
- In-flight streams remain pinned to their originally chosen partition (per rollback ADR) to avoid mid-stream model swap.

6) Performance constraints
- Routing decision must be cheap (no per-request control-plane calls). Use cached rollout snapshot with periodic refresh.
- Avoid adding high-cardinality labels beyond the telemetry allowlist (stage_id ok; do not include arbitrary plan names).

Implementation plan
A) Data model / config plumbing
- Extend routing config for Dedicated pools to include optional rollout context:
  - rollout_enabled flag (feature-gated)
  - stage_id and stage definition
  - stable_target + canary_target handles (already exist for “two target” rollouts in Hosted; Dedicated adds partitions)

B) Partition selection logic
- Introduce a “partition chooser” in routing layer:
  - Input: pool_id, stage, request/session identifiers, selected region
  - Output: {partition=stable|canary, reason}
- Support both percent-based and replica-based stage definitions:
  - percent: choose canary if hash_bucket < percent
  - replica: choose canary if canary partition exists AND canary_size >= min_replicas; then optionally cap to derived percent to avoid overload (per infra guidelines)

C) Health/saturation guardrails
- Query local region signals (already used for overload protection) to determine if canary is eligible.
- If canary ineligible, fall back to stable and tag bypass reason:
  - canary_missing
  - canary_unhealthy
  - canary_saturated
  - telemetry_stale (if gating data is too old and policy is fail-closed)

D) Multi-region
- Keep region selection separate from stage selection:
  1) region selection (existing)
  2) stage partition decision within region
- Ensure both stable/canary targets have per-region endpoints; if canary missing in chosen region, treat as “canary_missing” and route stable.

E) Feature flag + gradual enablement
- Gate behavior behind dedicated_staged_rollouts_routing flag scoped by account/pool/region.
- Default off; enabled for dogfood pools and beta design partners only.

Testing
- Unit tests:
  - deterministic hashing for session_id
  - percent boundary conditions (1%, 10%, 50%, 100%)
  - replica-based stages on small pools
  - canary bypass behavior under simulated saturation
  - multi-region: missing canary in one region doesn’t cause cross-region canary routing
- Integration tests (owned by ENG-5995/PR-28610, but we add harness hooks):
  - create plan -> stage 1% -> verify ~1% canary attribution -> force canary unhealthy -> verify stable fallback with bypass metrics

Rollout / observability
- Add metrics (names illustrative; final names in telemetry ticket):
  - dedicated.routing.partition_selected{pool_id, region, partition, stage_id}
  - dedicated.routing.canary_bypass{pool_id, region, stage_id, reason}
- Confirm dashboards in observability-pack pick up partition/stage tags.

Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Should canary traffic be allowed to spill cross-region if local canary is missing?
  - Decision: No by default; only if existing Dedicated spillover policy is enabled AND plan explicitly allows (v1: plan-level boolean; future: per-stage/per-region).
- Q: What identifier to hash for stickiness?
  - Decision: Prefer session_id/conversation_id when present; otherwise request_id.

Deliverables
- Routing layer change implementing stage-based partition selection + guardrails.
- Unit tests + metrics emitted for selection/bypass reasons.
- Feature flag support for scoped enablement.

Linked work
- GitHub PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-28503-routing-split-by-stage-for-dedicated-pools.json (implementation + unit tests)
- Telemetry tags PR (dependency): sources/github/redwood/pr-28521-emit-stage-tags-in-metrics-and-traces.json
- Incident learnings (capacity starvation): sources/slack/incidents/1738803100-incident-beta-rollout-partition-caused-429s.json

Progress / updates
- 2025-02-10 (Mina Haddad): Aligned with Infra (Irene/Vanessa) that v1 must enforce min stable headroom; replica-based stages required for <= 8-GPU pools.
- 2025-02-18 (Emily Zhao): Implemented partition chooser behind feature flag; added bypass reasons and stable-first behavior for missing canary in-region.
- 2025-02-24 (Ravi Menon): Review: ensure hashing uses stage_id in salt to prevent reusing old canary cohort across stage promotions.
- 2025-03-03 (Peter Holtz): Added additional overload guardrail: if stable partition 429 rate > threshold, force all traffic to stable (ignore canary percent) until recovered.
- 2025-03-07 (Emily Zhao): Merged PR-28503; validated on dogfood pool in us-east-1 + eu-west-1; observed correct ~10% canary selection and stable fallback when canary drained.

Completion notes
- Marking Done after merge + dogfood verification. Remaining follow-ups tracked elsewhere:
  - confirm dashboards/alerts consume canary_bypass reason (ENG-5966)
  - console surface of bypass events as “evidence” for gate failures (ENG-5980)
  - document multi-region spillover semantics in operator runbook (runbook ticket)
comments: 2025-02-12 — Jordan Lee: Please ensure partition choice is deterministic across router instances. Avoid any per-instance randomization; use consistent hashing only.

2025-02-20 — Vanessa Ortiz: Strongly recommend blocking canary selection if canary partition < 2 replicas in-region. We saw queue depth spikes when canary was a single node and got all ‘unlucky’ long prompts.
2025-02-27 — Sean Gallagher: Add an explicit metric for ‘canary_missing’ vs ‘canary_unhealthy’—we need to distinguish provisioning lag from actual regression during beta.
2025-03-05 — Kaitlyn Nguyen: No additional auth changes needed at routing layer, but confirm feature flag scoping respects account boundaries (no cross-tenant leakage in cached snapshots).
2025-03-10 — Mina Haddad: Thanks—this unblocks end-to-end staged rollouts beta. Please keep an eye on the 429 regression ticket (SUP-28522) to ensure bypass reasons show up in dashboards.
